subject: Full Bayes Correlated Topic Models from manual

messages.author: 4200afc0918e2941
messages.subject: Full Bayes Correlated Topic Models from manual
parts:
Hi list. Not sure if this is a typo in the manual or if I'm missing
something obvious. I'm trying to adjust the soft K means example
(src/models/misc/cluster/soft-k-means) to have a prior on the
covariance, as in the Full Bayes Correlated Topic model on page 76 of
the manual. The line I'm wondering about is:

Sigma <- sigma' * Omega * sigma;

Error from stanc:

--- Translating Stan graphical model to C++ code ---
bin/stanc src/models/misc/cluster/soft-k-means/soft-k-means2.stan
--o=src/models/misc/cluster/soft-k-means/soft-k-means2.cpp
Model name=soft_k_means2_model
Input file=src/models/misc/cluster/soft-k-means/soft-k-means2.stan
Output file=src/models/misc/cluster/soft-k-means/soft-k-means2.cpp

INVALID COMMAND-LINE ARGUMENT
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION:
file=src/models/misc/cluster/soft-k-means/soft-k-means2.stan; line=19,
column=3

Sigma <- sigma' * Omega * sigma;
^-- here


DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
base type mismatch in assignment; left variable=Sigma; left base
type=matrix; right base type=real
binary infix operator <= with functional interpretation logical_lt
requires arguments or primitive type (int or real), found left
type=matrix, right arg type=real; no matches for function
name="logical_lt"
arg 0 type=matrix
arg 1 type=real
Parser expecting: "}"

Execute "stanc --help" for more information

In the manual, and in my code (attached and pasted below), sigma is a
vector of length K, so indeed the right-hand side = sigma' * Omega *
sigma which is a scalar, while the left-hand side is supposed to be a
K by K matrix. Should this perhaps be Sigma <- diag_matrix(sigma) *
Omega * diag_matrix(sigma);? (Is this correct/efficient?)

Thanks!
Seth

--
data {
int<lower=0> N; // number of data points
int<lower=1> D; // number of dimensions
int<lower=1> K; // number of clusters
vector[D] y[N]; // observations
}
transformed data {
real<upper=0> neg_log_K;
neg_log_K <- -log(K);
}
parameters {
vector[D] mu[K]; // cluster means
corr_matrix[D] Omega; // correlation matrix
vector<lower=0>[D] sigma; // scales
}
transformed parameters {
cov_matrix[D] Sigma; // covariance matrix
real<upper=0> soft_z[N,K]; // log unnormalized cluster assigns
Sigma <- sigma' * Omega * sigma;
for (n in 1:N)
for (k in 1:K)
soft_z[n,k] <- neg_log_K - 0.5 * dot_self(mu[k] - y[n]);
}
model {
for (k in 1:K)
mu[k] ~ normal(0,1); // prior
for (n in 1:N)
lp__ <- lp__ + log_sum_exp(soft_z[n]); // likelihood
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Full Bayes Correlated Topic Models from manual
parts:
Doh! I dropped in a quadratic form where I
wanted a rescaling. This can be written as a one-liner
as:

A more efficient way to do this is with iteration:

for (m in 1:D) {
Sigma[m,m] <- sigma[m] * sigma[m] * Omega[m,n];
for (n in (m+1):D) {
Sigma[m,n] <- sigma[m] * sigma[n] * Omega[m,n];
}
}

You could also use a (scaled) inverse Wishart prior.

I'll fix it for the next manual and thank you for the heads
up.

- Bob
